      "arc_elbow_guided_component_recoloring": {
        "id": "arc_elbow_guided_component_recoloring",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Infer component recoloring from large elbow-shaped color cues (general, v3)",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a large monochrome L/elbow object, use its color as the paint color for one other entire component. Infer the target from all demonstrations rather than assuming the nearest component is selected. In a demonstrated case, identify repeated non-background components with identical normalized footprints (same cell offsets from their bounding-box origins, preserving orientation), then use the elbow’s concave quadrant and the components’ relative placement to determine which copy is targeted: recolor the matching copy on the exterior side of the elbow’s concave quadrant, opposite the inside of the L, while preserving its identical counterpart on the inside. A solved example used a color-1 elbow and two identical color-3 footprints at rows 13–16/columns 10–15 and rows 21–24/columns 23–28; the upper-left, exterior-side copy was recolored 1 and the other was unchanged. Caution: a plausible nearby component selected only by distance is not sufficient. Compare component footprints across the grid, establish their relative placement to the elbow, and verify the rule against every demonstration before applying it. Preserve all cells outside the selected component.",

      "arc_partitioned_tile_marker_count_encoding": {
        "id": "arc_partitioned_tile_marker_count_encoding",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Encode marker counts in separator-partitioned ARC tiles",
        "content": "For ARC grids partitioned by full-width and full-height separator lines, treat each rectangular region between separators as a tile and produce one output cell per tile. Identify each tile's background color and sparse marker color from the grid, then count marker cells. In validated examples, a tile with exactly two markers maps to output color 1, while a tile with exactly one marker maps to that tile's background color (which may vary by task, such as 5 or 3). Do not hard-code color 5 for one-marker tiles. Infer any other count-to-output mappings from demonstrations rather than extrapolating. Example: background 3, marker 2, tile counts [[2,2],[1,1],[2,1]] produced [[1,1],[3,3],[1,3]]. Validate separator boundaries, per-tile counts, and output shape against the demonstrations.",

      "arc_opposite_edge_bar_marker_beams": {
        "id": "arc_opposite_edge_bar_marker_beams",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Propagate marker beams between opposite edge bars in ARC grids",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a uniform background, two long straight bars on opposite edges, and sparse marker cells of a third color, infer beam directions and segment-relative offset mapping from the geometry and demonstrations rather than assuming a fixed orientation. Keep edge-bar cells unchanged. In validated examples, sparse markers are recolored to 4, while each marker sends a straight beam in its original color through the background toward the aligned edge bar; fill only the cells between marker and bar, preserving cells on the other side unless the demonstrated projection rule selects them. Markers can also select parallel rows or columns on the opposite bar: measure each marker's offset along its source bar segment, copy that offset to the opposite bar's segment, then extend a ray inward from that segment. This can produce strokes in a disjoint row/column segment, including across the grid to the far edge where no bar is present. Extend projected rays all the way to the grid boundary, including the boundary cell when it is not itself part of a bar; preserve only actual bar cells. Validate both endpoints explicitly so no background gap remains at an unoccupied opposite edge. Validated variant: on an 11x7 grid with background 5, color-0 left bar at column 0 rows 4–6, color-0 right bar at column 6 rows 0–2, and color-7 markers at (4,3) and (5,3), recolor markers to 4; fill color 7 at columns 1–2 of rows 4–5 toward the left bar; marker offsets 0 and 1 within the left segment select rows 0 and 1 within the right segment, where color 7 fills columns 0–5, preserving the right-bar cells at column 6. Other validated examples establish the same principle for vertical side bars and marker offsets. Another validated case: on a 22x18 grid with background 9, color-0 bars at row 0 columns 3–4 and row 21 columns 16–17, and a color-1 marker at (5,3), recolor the marker to 4; fill color 1 at (1–4,3) toward the top bar, and map offset 0 from the top segment to column 16 of the bottom segment, extending the projected ray through to row 0 column 16 because that cell is not part of a bar. Confirm orientation, source segment, offset mapping, beam direction, and exact fill extent from examples; do not force this rule onto differently arranged bars without evidence.",

        "title": "arc_three_band_horizontal_mirror_tiling",
        "content": "For ARC inputs of size H×W with arbitrary cell colors, a demonstrated transform creates a 3H×2W output using horizontal reflection and three vertical bands. For each source row, form reverse(row) + row (the left half is the horizontal mirror and the right half is unchanged). Stack source rows in this order: reversed input row order for the top band, original row order for the middle band, and reversed input row order for the bottom band. Thus the top/bottom bands are vertically reversed copies, while the middle band keeps the original row order. Validate dimensions and band order. Demonstrated on a 9×3 input producing 27×6; also solved a 6×15 test as 18×30 with a correct submission.",

Derivation from demo: input [[8,8,3,6],[8,8,4,9],[0,8,8,5],[2,0,7,8]] output quadrants matched unchanged/CW/CCW/180. Don't confuse clockwise and counterclockwise rows; compute using explicit matrix rotations and verify all quadrants before submitting.",

      "arc_opposite_edge_bar_marker_beams_segment_offset_mapping": {
        "id": "arc_opposite_edge_bar_marker_beams_segment_offset_mapping",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC opposite-edge bar marker beams with segment-offset mapping",
        "content": "For ARC grids with a uniform background, two equal-length solid bars on opposite borders, and sparse interior markers, use the bars as parallel beam anchors. A marker's coordinate along the bar span determines its corresponding coordinate on the opposite bar span by preserving the offset from the start of each span. On the marker side, replace each marker with color 4 and fill the straight segment from it to the nearby bar using the marker color, leaving the bar intact. At the corresponding offset on the opposite bar, extend a full perpendicular line from that border bar toward the far border, in the marker color; preserve the source bar. This works in either orientation: vertical side bars produce horizontal beams, and top/bottom bars produce vertical beams. Demonstrations: vertical bars and markers colored 9 produced 4 at each marker, 9 between markers and nearby bars, plus full 9 lines at mapped offsets across the opposite bar's region. A separate case with color 3 showed a single marker projecting a full line at the same relative row offset. Validate segment lengths, span ordering, and untouched bar cells. Additional confirmed case: task-09dd336d used 14x11 background 7, top border bar color 2 at row 0 columns 3–5, bottom border bar at row 13 columns 0–2, and color-3 markers at (3,4), (7,3), (7,5). Correct output changed the markers to 4; filled vertical color-3 segments from the top bar to each marker (at columns 4 rows 1–2, and columns 3 and 5 rows 1–6); and projected full vertical color-3 lines in the bottom bar's mapped offsets, columns 0–2, rows 0–12, preserving both bars. A first attempted answer omitted the source-bar-to-marker segments and was incorrect, confirming those connecting segments are essential in addition to projected beams.",

      "arc_separator_grid_junction_block_encoding_f362c6ff": {
        "id": "arc_separator_grid_junction_block_encoding_f362c6ff",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Compress separator-grid junctions using uniform 2×2 blocks (task-f362c6ff)",
        "content": "For ARC tasks like task-f362c6ff, sample the colors at every horizontal/vertical separator intersection, including boundary lines, to form a junction matrix. Remove only contiguous outermost rows or columns whose entries are all the separator/background color; do not trim uniform rows or columns in the interior. For each overlapping 2×2 block of the remaining matrix, output its common color if all four junctions match; otherwise output the interior tile/background color. The output has one fewer row and column than the trimmed junction matrix. Infer colors from the input and demonstrations. Validated example: junction columns c=[2,8,14,20,26] and rows r=[0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21]. After removing the top and bottom all-4 rows, 2×2 block reduction yields [[7,7,0,0],[5,7,7,7],[5,5,7,9],[7,5,7,9],[7,5,7,9]]. Directly submitting a sampled junction matrix is incorrect; perform the overlapping-block reduction. Another confirmed example used junction matrix [[6,6,8,8],[6,6,8,8]]; trimming the two rightmost all-8 columns left [[6,6]], producing [[6]]. Demonstrations also support mixed blocks taking the interior color. Validate sampling coordinates, trim only qualifying outer boundaries, and check every output block.\n\nAdditional solved test: separator rows r=[0,5,10,15,20] and columns c=[0,6,12,18,24] gave junction matrix [[3,3,3,7,7],[6,6,3,7,7],[6,6,3,3,3],[3,1,1,8,8],[3,1,1,8,8]]. No outer row or column was all separator color 3, so no trimming applied. With interior color 2, overlapping 2×2 reduction produced [[2,2,2,7],[6,2,2,2],[2,2,2,2],[2,1,2,8]], confirmed correct. This supports keeping non-uniform edge rows/columns and using the interior tile color for every mixed block.\n\nAdditional confirmed test (task-f362c6ff): separator rows r=[0,8,16], columns c=[2,5,8,11,14,17,20,23], separator color 2, and interior color 9. Junction matrix was [[2,2,5,5,2,2,3,3],[2,2,5,5,5,5,3,3],[2,2,2,2,5,5,2,2]]. Trim the two leftmost outer columns because each is entirely separator color 2. The remaining 3x6 matrix reduces by overlapping 2x2 blocks to [[5,9,9,9,3],[9,9,5,9,9]], confirmed correct. This is a useful case where trimming changes output width; skipping the all-separator left border columns yields an incorrect answer. Uniform 2x2 blocks of the separator color do output that color when they remain after trimming, as shown by demonstrations.\n\nUnresolved failure note (current 24x28 variant): input has apparent separator rows r=[1,4,7,10,13,16,19,22], columns c=[3,7,11,15,19,23,27], line color 9, and interior tiles of color 1. The apparent junction matrix is [[9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,9,9,9,9],[9,9,9,4,4,3,3],[5,5,4,4,4,3,3],[5,5,4,4,8,8,9],[5,5,9,9,8,8,8],[4,4,7,7,8,8,8],[4,4,7,7,8,8,8]]. This sample-coordinate interpretation and its reductions were wrong on the test. Rejected guesses included: full 7x6 reductions with background 9; full reductions with background 1 (both preserving and remapping uniform 9 blocks); cropped 5x6 reductions (both backgrounds); and a 6x6 variant retaining one empty top row. The 8 demos still strongly support overlapping 2x2 uniform-corner reduction, but for this layout re-derive which rows/columns are actual junction lines and how boundary/padding rows are handled before submitting. Do not reuse the failed 5x6 matrix above as validated output.",

        "content": "For this ARC task family, given an input grid A with H rows and W columns, horizontally expand each row r to E-row = r[::-1] + r. Let E be the resulting H-row grid. The output is E[::-1] + E + E[::-1]: three vertical bands in reversed source-row order, original source-row order, then reversed source-row order. Output dimensions are 3H×2W. Do not substitute E + E[::-1] + E. This rule matches the received 5×13 demonstration (15×26 output) and solved the 8×7 test. It was also accepted on a 6×2 input consisting entirely of color 8, producing an 18×4 output entirely of 8; this confirms dimensions and the uniform-grid case. To avoid manual transcription errors, generate the full output and verify it has 3H rows and 2W columns, and that the band row orders are reversed/original/reversed. Retain the previously validated width-1 behavior without generalizing beyond this task family.",

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Stamp the full demonstrated motif at markers (task-8ceb4c33)",
        "content": "For task-8ceb4c33 variants, identify the uniform background, seed/template, and isolated target markers from the current grid. Take the seed's non-background bounding box as the complete template rectangle; its geometric center is the anchor, which may be a foreground-colored or background-colored cell. Keep the original seed and stamp the full rectangle in the same orientation centered on each isolated marker, replacing that marker with the template value at the anchor. Copy background-colored cells inside the template too; treat color 0 as foreground whenever it differs from the background. Infer colors, shape, orientation, background, and marker color anew for each instance rather than reusing a previous motif. Validated instance: background 6, template [[1,0,6],[0,3,0],[9,6,6]] with anchor 3, and nine isolated color-5 markers; stamping centered on each marker was accepted. Execution caution: check each marker's exact row/column and anchor alignment when generating or transcribing the output. A one-column shift in one stamp caused an incorrect submission; the aligned grid was accepted.",
